Appeals Department  
[Appeals mailing address or fax number from Anthem instructions]

Re: First-level appeal of adverse benefit determination  
Member: Morgan Foster  
Member ID: W276906709  
Requested service: Partial knee replacement  
CPT: 27446  
Reference number: POC-EED29F7594-68772  
Date of denial notice: August 11, 2026

Dear Appeals Reviewer:

I am appealing Anthem’s denial of prior authorization for partial knee replacement, CPT 27446. The denial states that the imaging findings submitted did not support medical necessity.

The submitted clinical record supports the requested procedure:

- The patient has experienced 14 months of progressive knee pain that has not improved with rest.
- The patient completed 16 weeks of supervised physical therapy focused on quadriceps strengthening and range of motion, including 24 visits from February 25, 2026, through June 17, 2026. The physical therapy discharge note documents completion of this treatment.
- NSAID treatment for four months produced inadequate relief.
- A corticosteroid injection on March 26, 2026, provided only two weeks of partial relief.
- MRI performed on June 27, 2026, showed full-thickness cartilage loss in the medial compartment with bone-on-bone apposition. The medial compartment was graded Kellgren-Lawrence grade 4.
- The patient cannot climb stairs without assistance and wakes three to four times nightly because of pain.
- Examination showed positive provocative testing on the affected side and range of motion limited by pain.
- The record does not identify active infection or untreated substance use. The patient’s BMI is 29 and the patient is a nonsmoker.

The MRI demonstrates advanced, localized medial-compartment joint destruction, including full-thickness cartilage loss and bone-on-bone contact. These findings directly address the stated basis for denial. The imaging is not merely suggestive of mild or nonspecific disease; it documents severe structural loss in the compartment targeted by the requested partial knee replacement. The objective imaging findings are also consistent with the patient’s persistent pain, restricted motion, sleep disruption, and substantial functional limitations.

The patient has also completed substantial nonoperative treatment without adequate or durable relief. Physical therapy, NSAIDs, and injection treatment have failed to restore function or control symptoms. Continued conservative treatment has therefore not provided a reasonable resolution of the patient’s documented condition.

I respectfully request that Anthem overturn the denial and approve CPT 27446. Please have the request reviewed by an orthopedic surgeon or other qualified clinician who has not made the initial denial. If Anthem maintains the denial, please provide the complete medical-necessity policy and clinical review criteria applied to this request, including the exact imaging requirements, the version and effective date used, the clinical rationale for concluding that the June 27, 2026 MRI was insufficient, and the qualifications of the reviewing clinician.

I have not quoted Anthem’s medical-necessity policy because the denial notice did not identify that policy, and the publicly available materials reviewed did not establish which policy or criteria Anthem applied to this member’s request. This appeal is based on the clinical records and the documented denial reason.

Please confirm receipt of this appeal and notify me of the appeal determination in writing.

Sincerely,

Morgan Foster  
[Mailing address]  
[Telephone number]  
[Email address]

Enclosures:

- Medication and injection treatment history
- Orthopedic examination and surgical recommendation from Lindqvist, MD
- Other clinical records supporting medical necessity
